newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Rotterdam warehouses unaware of any hidden copper.
newsitem.headline: Rotterdam warehouses unaware of any hidden copper.

text.p: Rotterdam's metals storers on Wednesday said they had no knowledge of any "hidden" copper lying in the port's warehouses.

The World Bureau of Metal Statistics said in its latest monthly report that between 1990 and 1995 receipts of refined copper into bonded warehouses in the Netherlands had exceeded deliveries out by 588,000 tonnes.
"This is complete and utter nonsense," a spokesman for Steinweg, the port's main metals warehouser, told Reuters.
Another warehouse firm also involved in copper storage Hoogewerff de Rijke said it had no knowledge of the matter.
"This is the first I've heard about this," metals manager Simon Yntema said. "I have absolutely no knowledge of it."
The WBMS said in analysis based on data from the Dutch Bureau of Statistics and the London Metal Exchange the copper could be previously unrecorded stocks.

But the WBMS also noted that more than one million tonnes of copper coming from the former Soviet Union between 1991 and 1994 did not meet LME requirements and therefore could not be counted in LME stocks.
The delivery pattern also suggested China as the destination of a large volume of refined copper leaving the Netherlands in 1993 when there was no overall change in LME stocks.

Other factors behind the discrepency could be that some of the data refers to copper alloy ingots, or that as it coincides with the introduction of the single European market, it has fallen into a statistical black hole. --David Evans, Amsterdam Newsroom +31 20 504 5000
